key_insight: PhysMiner combines triple decomposition of velocity gradients with LLM-based reasoning to automatically identify turbulence mechanisms while reducing shear contamination.
engineering_relevance: The framework can improve turbulence diagnosis and model development for engineering flows by delivering more reliable physics discovery and better Reynolds-stress predictions.
method: Decomposes the velocity gradient tensor into rigid rotation, pure shearing, and normal straining components.
Uses a discover-physics agent to fuse statistics, spatial structures, and literature knowledge for inference.
Adds a review agent and an evolving Triple Decomposition Library for validation and cross-case learning.
evidence_signal: The authors report validation across five benchmarks and an end-to-end demonstration on periodic hill flow, where the system produced turbulence-modeling recommendations and an improved subgrid-scale model.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of automated reasoning and benchmark coverage, so broader testing is needed before general deployment on diverse turbulent flows.
paper_title: PhysMiner: An Agentic AI Framework for Discovering Turbulence Physics
